title: Sales enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Deck Guidance, Pricing, Case Studies, Security FAQ
author: Asha Banerjee
body:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook equips sales, solutions, and pre-sales teams with standardized positioning, competitive battlecards, pitch-deck guidance, pricing talking points, short case studies, and a prospect-facing Security FAQ. Use the artifacts and messaging below for discovery calls, executive briefings, and procurement/Security reviews.

Audience: Sales reps, AE/SDR motions, Solutions Engineers, Customer Engineering, Sales Enablement.

Core product calls used in messaging:
- Redwood API (hosted inference)
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity / SLA-backed)
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem deployments)
- Redwood Console (observability + operations)
- Redwood Optimize (cost/performance toolkit)

1) Positioning & elevator pitches

One-line elevator: Redwood Inference delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM inference for production — across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — with first-class observability and rollout controls that reduce risk and unit cost.

Problem statements we sell to:
- "We can't predict inference cost or latency as usage scales."
- "Our vendors force us into single deployment modes that don't meet compliance or latency needs."
- "Quality regressions after model updates break client UX because we lack evaluation and rollout tooling."

Core value messages (3 pillars):
- Predictable economics: usage controls, batching, cache, and quantization recommendations from Redwood Optimize reduce per-token cost while preserving quality.
- Production-grade reliability: SLAs, automated fallbacks, topology-aware routing, and canary rollouts keep features live under load or regional outages.
- Deployment flexibility & control: same API and tooling across hosted, dedicated, and private environments to meet security and residency constraints.

Persona-specific messages:
- Engineering/ML: "Drop-in runtime, KV/prefix cache, auto-batching, and kernel selection reduce integration friction and improve p99 latency."
- Platform team: "Centralized routing, quotas, and cost breakdowns per token/route enforce governance across teams."
- Security/Compliance: "VPC/offline packages, customer-managed keys, audit logs, and RBAC simplify audits and vendor assessments."

2) Competitive brief / battlecard (short)

Competitor categories: Managed Cloud AI, LLM API Providers, Self-hosted Inference Runtimes.

Key customer objections and rebuttals:
- "Why not use large cloud AI provider?"
  - Rebuttal: Redwood focuses on inference economics and consistent behavior across deployment modes. While hyperscalers offer model access, Redwood adds deploy-time controls, transparent unit economics, and fallbacks to preserve uptime and QoE.
- "Why not self-host an inference runtime?"
  - Rebuttal: Self-host projects often underestimate the ops cost (kernel selection, batching, KV cache correctness, load-shed policies). Redwood provides a battle-tested runtime plus orchestration and SRE tooling — lower TCO and faster time-to-production.
- "Why use Redwood over other API-first LLM providers?"
  - Rebuttal: Redwood's differentiation is the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private plus observability integrated with cost and quality monitoring (per-token cost traces, per-route dashboards, regression alerts).

Battlecard quick facts (use in rebuttal):
- Latency: tuned kernels + continuous batching \u2192 p50/p95 reductions vs naive hosts. Quote example: customers see 20\u201360% p95 latency improvement after switching to Redwood Dedicated for throughput workloads.
- Cost controls: batching, prefix caching, and per-route caching reduce effective token consumption; customers reported 30% token cost reduction on average after Optimize recommendations.
- Security: private deployments, customer-managed KMS/HSM, audit logs, SAML/SCIM, VPC peering support.

3) Pitch deck outline & speaker notes (recommended 10\u201312 slides)

Slide 1 \u2014 Title: Redwood Inference: Predictable, production LLM inference - Speaker note: One-line elevator + quick proof of credibility (team + scale).
Slide 2 \u2014 The problem: rising inference costs, reliability gaps, fragmentation between dev and infra - Speaker note: Use prospect-specific examples gathered in discovery.
Slide 3 \u2014 Our product: what we ship (API, Dedicated, Private, Console, Optimize)
Slide 4 \u2014 How it works (high-level): runtime, smart routing, caching, model catalog
Slide 5 \u2014 Economics: batching, caching, quantization, per-route cost control (include sample table)
Slide 6 \u2014 Reliability & operations: SLAs, fallbacks, canary rollouts, tracing
Slide 7 \u2014 Security & compliance: VPC, KMS, audit logs, SSO, data residency
Slide 8 \u2014 Integrations & partner ecosystem: cloud regions, KMS providers, observability hooks
Slide 9 \u2014 Case studies: 2 brief customer ROI stories (see below)
Slide 10 \u2014 Pricing & procurement path: hosted vs dedicated vs private summary + next steps
Slide 11 \u2014 Implementation plan & timeline: pilot \u2192 production \u2192 rollout
Slide 12 \u2014 Ask: pilot terms, POC scope, next meeting

Speaker guidance: keep slides visual; use sample token cost charts and latency percentiles. Bring an SE to technical execs; bring security lead for any compliance-sensitive prospect.

4) Pricing guidance (how to position pricing conversations)

Pricing models summary:
- Hosted API: usage-based (per-token generation/embedding units) for rapid self-serve adoption and POC.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity (monthly/annual commits) for predictable throughput and reduced unit cost.
- Private: license and platform fee + support tiers for on-prem / VPC deployments.
- Add-ons: extended observability retention, premium SLA, security/compliance packages.

Negotiation priorities by buyer:
- Developer-first teams: prioritize self-serve hosted credits and quick onboarding offers.
- Platform/Enterprise: prioritize committed Dedicated capacity, predictable pricing, and enterprise support add-on (SLA).
- Regulated buyers: emphasize Private deployment pricing and professional services for deployment and attestations.

Sample internal pricing cheat-sheet (talking points for AE):
- Small POC (team-level): free credits + low-volume hosted usage; emphasize time-to-value.
- Production scale (predictable latency/high throughput): propose Dedicated with 6\u201312 month commit and quarterly cost reviews.
- Regulated/High-risk: Private + onboarding services; expect 3\u20136 month integration period.

5) Short case studies (sales one-pagers)

Case Study: AcmeDocs (SaaS documentation platform)
- Problem: inconsistent model latency, rising inference bill, and occasional quality regressions after model swaps.
- Solution: Migrated key endpoints to Redwood Dedicated + used Redwood Optimize recommendations (caching and quantization).
- Results: 45% reduction in per-token bill on high-volume endpoints, p95 latency reduced from 420ms to 180ms, deployment rollouts reduced errors by 92% using canary policies.
- Timeline: pilot (4 weeks), Dedicated onboarding (6 weeks), production (ongoing).

Case Study: FinBank (regional bank, regulated)
- Problem: needed private deployment for PII-sensitive workflows and predictable SLAs for customer-facing chat.
- Solution: Private deployment in a dedicated VPC + customer-managed KMS, audit logging, RBAC integration (SAML/SCIM).
- Results: Met regulatory review within 8 weeks; average query latency stable at 230ms p95; vendors consolidated, projected 18% TCO reduction vs prior in-house infra.

6) Security FAQ for prospects (brief, to include in sales packet)

Q: Where does customer data reside for Hosted API?
A: Hosted API data is processed in the selected cloud region and retained according to our data retention policy. Customers with residency or retention requirements should evaluate Redwood Dedicated or Private deployments.

Q: Do you support customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs)?
A: Yes. For Dedicated and Private deployments we support CMKs via cloud KMS integrations and HSM-based key wrapping where required. Hosted API customers can request bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options for enterprise plans.

Q: Is traffic encrypted in transit and at rest?
A: Yes. All network traffic uses TLS 1.2+; data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Logs and audit trails are stored encrypted and access-controlled.

Q: Can we deploy Redwood within our VPC or on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports deployment into customer VPCs and an on-prem appliance option where air-gap requirements exist. Private includes options for log forwarding and local observability integrations.

Q: What certifications and audits do you have?
A: Redwood maintains an internal compliance program. We currently hold SOC 2 Type II (expected for many orgs) — if SOC 2 is a gating requirement, reference the latest compliance pack and roadmap; for enterprise customers we provide evidence and are able to include customers in audit windows where contractually required. (Check /confluence/security-and-compliance for the current attestation artifacts.)

Q: How do you handle access control and identity management?
A: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning, role-based access control in the Console, and per-route API keys or token scoping to isolate usage. Dedicated/Private can integrate with customer IAM.

Q: How do you handle logging and monitoring for security incidents?
A: Redwood provides audit logs, request traces, and error dashboards in Redwood Console. For Private deployments, logs can be forwarded to the customer SIEM. We provide incident response SLAs and can work through security questionnaires during procurement.

8) Recommended play actions (next steps for AEs)
1) Customize slide deck for prospect: swap in prospect metrics and tighten ROI slides.
2) Engage SE for a 60\u201390 minute technical briefing for interested platform/security teams.
3) Offer scoped pilot: 4\u20138 week POC with clear success criteria (latency targets, cost targets, accuracy/quality tests).
4) If security sensitive, schedule vendor security review and share the Security Pack.
